title: Echo in the Vault
statement:
The castle vault logs every coin's serial number in the order it was deposited. A cursed 'echo coin' is a serial number that appears more than once. Given a list of integers `nums`, return True if any value appears at least twice, and False if every value is distinct.

Constraints:
- 0 <= len(nums) <= 10^5
- -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
hint: A set remembers everything it has seen in O(1) per lookup. Walk the list once and ask the set before you add.

title: Mirror Runes
statement:
Two rune-words are 'mirror runes' if one can be formed by rearranging the letters of the other, using every letter exactly once. Given two lowercase strings `s` and `t`, return True if `t` is a mirror rune of `s`, else False.

Constraints:
- 0 <= len(s), len(t) <= 5 * 10^4
- s and t consist of lowercase English letters
hint: Count each letter's occurrences in both words (a dict or collections.Counter) and compare the counts.

title: The Treasure Pair
statement:
The dragon's hoard is a row of chests, each holding `nums[i]` gold. Exactly one pair of chests together holds precisely `target` gold. Return the indices of that pair as a list `[i, j]` with `i < j`. You may not use the same chest twice.

Constraints:
- 2 <= len(nums) <= 10^4
- Exactly one valid answer exists
hint: As you scan, store each value's index in a hash map. For each chest, check whether (target - value) is already in the map.

title: The Lone Rune
statement:
Every rune in the ruins was carved twice by the ancients — except one, carved only once. Given a list of integers `nums` where every element appears exactly twice except for one element that appears once, return the lone element.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(nums) <= 3 * 10^4
- Exactly one element appears once; all others appear exactly twice
hint: A frequency dict works. For bonus style: XOR of the whole list cancels every pair and leaves the loner.

title: Crowd Favorite
statement:
The village votes for its favorite gladiator by number. Given a list of votes `nums`, return the number that appears most often. If several numbers tie for the most votes, return the smallest of them.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5
- -10^6 <= nums[i] <= 10^6
hint: Build a count dict, then pick the entry with the best (count, -value) — or compare (count, value) choosing higher count, then lower value.

title: Top of the Hoard
statement:
The dragon ranks its treasures by how many copies it owns. Given a list of integers `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` distinct values that occur most frequently. The answer may be returned in any order; it is guaranteed to be unique.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5
- 1 <= k <= number of distinct values
hint: Count with a dict, then sort the distinct values by count descending and slice the first k (or use a heap of size k).

title: Alchemy of Products
statement:
An alchemist brews one potion per ingredient: the potion's strength is the product of every OTHER ingredient's potency. Given a list of integers `nums`, return a list `answer` where `answer[i]` equals the product of all elements of `nums` except `nums[i]`. Division is forbidden by the alchemists' guild.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^4
- -30 <= nums[i] <= 30
hint: Two sweeps: prefix products left-to-right, then multiply by suffix products right-to-left.

title: The Vanished Page
statement:
A spellbook's pages are numbered 0 through n, but one page has been torn out. Given a list `nums` containing n distinct numbers taken from the range [0, n], return the one number missing from the range.

Constraints:
- 1 <= n <= 10^4
- All numbers in nums are distinct
hint: The full range's sum is n*(n+1)//2. Subtract the actual sum — the difference is the vanished page.

title: The Unbroken Chain
statement:
A chain of enchanted links only holds power if the link numbers run consecutively. Given an unsorted list of integers `nums`, return the length of the longest run of consecutive values (order in the list does not matter). Your solution should aim for O(n) time.

Constraints:
- 0 <= len(nums) <= 10^5
- -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
hint: Put everything in a set. A number starts a chain only if (number - 1) is absent; then walk forward counting.

title: The Hoard-Counter's Trial
statement:
BOSS TRIAL — The dragon demands a full audit. Given a list of integers `nums` (which may be negative) and an integer `k`, return the number of contiguous subarrays whose elements sum to exactly `k`.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(nums) <= 2 * 10^4
- -1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000
- -10^7 <= k <= 10^7

Beware: negatives mean sliding windows fail. The hoard rewards prefix wisdom.
hint: Keep a running prefix sum and a dict counting how often each prefix value has appeared. Each step, add count[prefix - k] to the answer.
